<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **33** documentable anchor(s).

**49** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 05a30e6ed0989d3fb604686db4f2a93093c52ad0`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 39 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **221** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **49** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 05a30e6ed0989d3fb604686db4f2a93093c52ad0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ae8cac67476a80e256c12f471f9501f31b70eee6` — the merge of head `77094fc2b1c396f093e2cbbd31b74e295aa05440` into base `05a30e6ed0989d3fb604686db4f2a93093c52ad0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ae8cac67476a80e256c12f471f9501f31b70eee6 && git checkout ae8cac67476a80e256c12f471f9501f31b70eee6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 05a30e6ed0989d3fb604686db4f2a93093c52ad0 77094fc2b1c396f093e2cbbd31b74e295aa05440 && git checkout -B drift-repro 05a30e6ed0989d3fb604686db4f2a93093c52ad0 && git merge --no-ff 77094fc2b1c396f093e2cbbd31b74e295aa05440

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 05a30e6ed0989d3fb604686db4f2a93093c52ad0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 05a30e6ed0989d3fb604686db4f2a93093c52ad0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6467fc7c6ac0fed98197332ecebf9b31210c884b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/record-currency-backfill.ts, packages/objectql/src/record-currency-backfill.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/home-amount-recompute.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-home-amount-projection.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/federated-injected-column-readers.test.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/record-currency-codes.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/record-currency-codes.test.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/recompute-home-amounts.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/recompute-home-amounts.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/record-currency-backfill-organizations.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/home-amount-projection.test.ts + packages/types/src/keyset-walk.ts, packages/objectql/src/federated-object.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-driver-read-scope.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-references-and-master-detail.ts (homeAmountOrganizationOf), packages/objectql/src/home-amount-projection.ts, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts (errorCodeFields), packages/qa/dogfood/test/default-organization.testkit.ts, @oclif/core 5.1.2 parser/validate.js (exclusive with defaulted flags); prose faces read but not reviewed: .changeset/30674-record-currency-backfill-per-organization.md, content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx, content/docs/data-modeling/currency.mdx (the docs-only head commit).

Claimed on comment 6673053638 (supersedes 6672989010 at f7b7814e; the head moved by the docs-only commit 6467fc7c6a, admitted by amendment 6672994537). Governing text: ruling 6670707546 letter C items A and 3, the card's Task list, ADR-0144 D8 rule 4. Read: the net diff against `main` at 447226b, the card and all its comments, the PR body (not trusted; the tree was judged), and the files above on `origin/main`.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The ruled narrowing, exactly.** `backfillRecordCurrencyCodes` with neither `organizationId` nor `allOrganizations` now walks once read-only (`walkCodelessRows(..., apply=false)`), counts per organization off each row's own `organization_id`, and throws `organizationsRefusal` when more than one named organization is met — `code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR'`, `status`/`httpStatus: 400`, `field: 'organizationId'`, `organizations` array with each organization's `scannedRecords`/`codeless`/`written`/skip counts. The throw precedes the apply walk, so no `engine.update` runs; it fires on a dry run as on `--apply`. The CLI prints the message, one line per organization (`codeless row(s) of N scanned`), the remedy naming `--org ID` and `--all-organizations`, and exits 1; under `--json` the envelope carries `code`, `httpStatus` and `organizations`. Right, and it is the shape the ruling orders. The condition "more than one organization" is read from the object's rows, not from `sys_organization`: an organization with no row of the object cannot receive a wrong code, so this reading is tighter than the card's wording while losing nothing the ruling protects. Right.
2. **Single-organization database unchanged.** With one named organization (rows naming none ride along), the unscoped path proceeds: the dry run returns the preview; the apply run walks again under the unscoped `{ isSystem: true }` context, exactly the write `main` makes (no `tenantId` on the update, pinned). `formatRecordCurrencyBackfillReport` prints the per-organization lines only when `allOrganizations` is set, and the scope phrase only for a scoped or all-organizations run, so an unscoped single-organization run prints byte-identical text to `main` (pinned, including the "no line containing 'organization'" assertion). Right. The only delta is a second read pass on an unscoped apply run; no public surface moves. Acceptable.
3. **Tenant-scoped walk scopes reads AND writes.** Under `organizationId` the find context and every `engine.update` context carry `{ isSystem: true, tenantId }` (ruling item A.1), and the keyset walk's `where` carries `{ organization_id: organizationId }`, which `keysetWalk.withCursor` AND-s with the seek predicate (`$and`), so the caller's filter is never overwritten by the cursor. The belt-and-braces is justified by `engine-driver-read-scope.test.ts`: under `single` a system read naming an organization reaches the driver with no tenant predicate (ADR-0131 D8), and a CLI boot resolves the posture from its own shell. The dogfood cells run under `single` and the scoped pin stays green only through the `where` (ablation 2 reds it on all three cells after a dist rebuild). Under `isolated` the pin asserts `tenantId` reaches the driver as well. The write side is by-id updates of rows the filtered walk returned, so no row of another organization is ever selected for writing. No cross-tenant leak. Right.
4. **`allOrganizations`** walks and writes under the unscoped system context, counts per organization, prints each organization's line. `organizationId` together with `allOrganizations`, or a blank `organizationId`, is refused with `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400 before `engine.find` is called (pinned: `driver.find` never called). `organizationId` on an object that stores no `organization_id` (`tenancy.enabled: false`, or a federated object that does not provision it, via `isFederatedUnprovisionedInjectedColumn`) is refused `INVALID_FIELD` / 400 `field: 'organization_id'` before any read. Right.
5. **CLI flags.** `org` and `all-organizations` are an oclif `exclusive` pair; `@oclif/core` 5.1.2 skips a flag set from its default when judging exclusivity, so `--org` alone passes and the pair together is a parse error, exit 2, before the probe, the prompt and the boot (pinned: `probeMigrationTarget`, `bootSchemaStack`, the backfill all uncalled). The CLI passes `organizationId: flags.org` (undefined when absent) and spreads `allOrganizations: true` only when the flag is on, so an unflagged run hands neither option and the engine decides by the rows. The `--apply` prompt names the scope. The command parses and prints; scope, counts and refusal are the engine's, so the B card's REST door reuses them. Right.
6. **`localization.currency` is never written, never read, by the backfill.** The diff adds no read of settings or `localization.*`; `resolvePair` still judges the operator's `--code` against `iso_4217_currency` and that code is the only value written. The card's optional reference display was not implemented, so the function reads nothing about currencies but the operator's code. ADR-0144 D8 rule 4 holds. Right.
7. **`recomputeHomeAmounts.organizationId`** (ruling item 3): the walk, `homeAmountReadsFor` and every update run under `tenantId`, the walk filters on `organization_id`, the report and the audit metadata carry `organizationId`; blank is refused `VALIDATION_FAILED` (the run's existing option-error code) and an object storing no `organization_id` is refused `INVALID_FIELD`, both before any read (pinned by the find counter). Without it the run covers every organization and is never refused (pinned). `homeAmountOrganizationOf` prefers the row's own `organization_id` over `context.tenantId`, so a scoped run converts each row under its own organization exactly as the unscoped run does. The `code_blank` remedy and header now name `--org`. Right; this is a pure widening.
8. **Public surface changes.** Widened: `RecordCurrencyBackfillOptions.organizationId?`, `.allOrganizations?`; `RecordCurrencyBackfillReport.organizationId`, `.allOrganizations`, `.organizations`; `HomeAmountRecomputeOptions.organizationId?`; `HomeAmountRecomputeReport.organizationId`; the `--org` / `--all-organizations` / `--org` flags; two new exported types from the module (not the barrel, see ③). The `--json` success envelope gains the report's new keys. Narrowed: only the unscoped multi-organization run, as declared. Nothing unrelated narrows: `invalidField` was refactored onto `refusalOf` with the same `INVALID_FIELD` / 400 / `httpStatus` envelope; the `federated-injected-column-readers` table gains two `skips` rows for the new `organization_id` read and its guard. Right.
9. **The metadata-protocol declaration (`none`)** is right: no `packages/spec/**`, no authorable surface or defaults baseline, no metadata shape; the moved surfaces are engine options and CLI flags.
10. **Docs commit 6467fc7c6a** (`content/docs/data-modeling/currency.mdx`, +8/−3): L144–149 now say the backfill runs once per organization with `--org ID`, that a run naming no organization on a multi-organization database is refused before any write and lists each organization's codeless count, and that `--all-organizations` writes the one code into every organization's rows; L370–371 replace the "writes into every organization's codeless rows" sentence with "give it `--org` for each organization's code". Both statements match the tree. Prose face, not reviewed, read for truth: holds.

### ② Semver level

Changeset grades `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/cli` `patch`; the PR body and the changeset both declare the clause-② line as `yes` with the `(narrowing)` arm and the metadata-protocol line as `none`. Under ruling A (2026-10-21, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` level axis) the level follows the metadata protocol alone: `none` requires every introduced entry `patch`, and a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` while keeping its BREAKING carriers — the `!` in the title, the **BREAKING** banner, and the ADR-0087 disposition. The `(narrowing)` arm is the fixed spelling `clause2-line.mjs` reads, so the queue guard and the ADR-0087 gate see the breaking signal. ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: the body carries no FROM→TO rewrite, no migration heading or table; the "Who moves, and the fix" bullet is an operator instruction (a choice of code per organization), not a mechanical rewrite of metadata or consumer code, so the category is honest. `Check Changeset` concluded success on f7b7814e; the head commit touches no changeset. Consistent.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **WIP commits without the trailer pair.** The four commits under f7b7814e carry no `Claude-Session:` / `Co-authored-by:` pair; the head commit 6467fc7c6a carries both. AGENTS.md (commit message rule) wants the pair on an agent commit; the dev declares the branch is pushed and not force-pushed, and that the pair belongs in the landing message. Answer: accepted as a landing-seat obligation, not a must-fix — the lane seat puts the pair in the squash message and does not rewrite the branch (landed history is not rewritten). Named here so the seat reads it before landing.
- **New types not on the objectql barrel.** `RecordCurrencyBackfillOrganization` and `RecordCurrencyBackfillOrganizationsRefusal` are exported from the module only; `packages/objectql/src/index.ts` names exports one by one and is outside the card's file surface. `RecordCurrencyBackfillReport` (on the barrel) now references the first structurally, so a consumer reaches it as `RecordCurrencyBackfillReport['organizations'][number]`; the CLI recognises the refusal by its `organizations` array. Answer: accepted; should-fix on the B card (REST door) when it needs the named types, as the dev proposed. No gate asks for them.
- **Optional currency reference display skipped.** The card says the refusal MAY show each organization's `localization.currency` beside its count. Not implemented; the backfill reads nothing about currencies. Answer: accepted — the MAY was not taken, and the safest reading of D8 rule 4 is the one shipped.
- **`open_questions`: none** in the dev report 6672951771. **Skills follow-up** declared `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` for `skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md` L174 is filed as #30740 (open); nothing under `skills/**` or `docs/adr/**` is in this diff, so the Tier H close-out stays where the card put it.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`: no off-relay login to name.

### ④ Design judgment

- **The refusal pin is real.** `record-currency-backfill.test.ts` "two organizations and no scope" asserts the thrown `code`, `status`, `httpStatus`, `field`, the full `organizations` array with both organizations' counts, the message, `driver.update` never called, `d.writes` empty, and the stored rows still codeless — on dry and apply alike. Ablation 1 (the `named.length` threshold raised from greater-than-1 to greater-than-999) reds it; the pin cannot pass if the refusal does not fire. Holds.
- **The scope pin is real.** The scoped pin asserts only `a1`/`a2` written, `b1` untouched, and that every `deal` find's `where` carries `organization_id: org_a`; under `isolated` it asserts `tenantId` on every driver find and the one update. Ablation 2 (the `where` removed) reds two objectql pins and, after a dist rebuild with the preflight marker confirmed, the dogfood scoped pin on better-sqlite3, sqlite-wasm and PostgreSQL. The first src-only dogfood ablation was correctly discarded as a false green. Holds.
- **The dogfood cells hold.** `record-currency-backfill-organizations.test.ts` seeds rows straight into the driver (an amount, no code, as a switched field leaves them), under the default `single` posture with `installDefaultOrganization`, one object per pin so counts are independent: refusal with zero writes read back through an unscoped `engine.find`, `--org` A then B with B's own code (`EUR`), all organizations, and the one-organization unchanged case. `home-amount-projection.test.ts` adds the recompute's `organizationId` on the same three cells, asserting A's stored amount untouched and then rewritten by the unscoped run. Holds.
- **The narrowing against the published spec on `main`.** `main`'s module comment promised "one run writes one code into every codeless row of the field"; the ruling retires that promise for multi-organization databases and the diff replaces it with an explicit `allOrganizations`, so the capability is not taken away, it is made explicit. The refusal is the spec's own (the ADR-0144 Open item 13 hazard the file's comment named). Holds.
- Should-fix (not blocking): when the unscoped preview walk is cut by `maxRecords` (`preview.truncated`), the "one organization" verdict is taken on a partial scan. The apply walk is capped identically and id-ordered, so it writes the same prefix the preview counted and no other organization's row, but a truncated preview should refuse or warn rather than proceed silently; today the report's `truncated` flag and the CLI's "Walk incomplete" line are the only signal. A one-line guard (`if (preview.truncated) throw ...` or a warning) closes it.
- Note: the refusal counts an organization by any row it holds, so an organization whose rows all already carry a code (codeless 0) still blocks an unscoped run. Within the ruled shape ("a database holding more than one organization"), and the listed `0 codeless row(s)` tells the operator so; not a defect.
- Note: the unscoped apply run reads every row twice (preview then write). Fine for a one-off migration; the live-writer caveat between the two walks is the one the occupancy gate already documents.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-erl0zi`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4cytLmJxfAmgPVjUbbW`

**VERDICT: PASS**
